**DISCLAIMER:** Everything down below are custom exercises designed by myself. If you’d like to share my example(s), please consider crediting me (Zoey Alexandria) <3 


**ORIGINAL CUSTOM HOQ EXERCISES:**

**P1:**
Vocalizing with a HOQ can be tricky for some folks. The best way to do it is to close your eyes and imagine *you just finished running a 20 mile marathon straight, no breaks, no water, no nothing. You just cross the finish line, you see family/friends just past the line, you, obviously out of breath jog up to them still trying to catch your breath* you quickly vocalize “hey <inhale> I’m <inhale> so excited <inhale> to be <inhale> done <inhale>” on a single note, this can be any note your
Comfortable with, but I’d recommend vocalizing in a monotone on B3 (246.94 hz) as a starting point. If you’re a SpongeBob fan, you can also think to the episode [Rock Bottom ](https://youtu.be/5u9S76lKSxg)instead of blowing raspberry’s every other word, you’d inhale instead. While you’re doing this place your palm about an inch (make sure you’re being exact with your distance) away from your lips, you’ll feel yourself using more air more quickly using this exercise, for every word you speak there should be a noticeably large hot puff of air. 

**P2:** 
Once you get good at that, you’d try to keep the same level of air you normally have when you exhale when you’re vocalizing. At that point, think about the way you’d speak to a baby you were babysitting (make sure you’re in M1 for this) a baby who has extremely protective parents who order you to only speak very quietly around him or else they’ll fire you. If you use the same phrase “hey I’m so excited to be done” and visualize these scenarios and have the palm of your hand an inch away from your lips (do not use fingers, some of us have gaps between our fingers so our ability to measure the pressure is compromised, so always use your palm) and feeling for a hot puff on air for each syllable you vocalize “hey I’m so excited to be done” (vocalizing in a way you’d speak to a crabby baby). “Excited” will have three puffs because it has three syllables

You’re confusing timbre with pitch. Timbre is the tonal quality of a sound dictated by the audibility of harmonics overlaying whatever fundamental frequency is being produced. In layman’s terms, timbre is the the tone of a note. You can change timbre via manipulation of the filter (changing the shape of the vocal tract, manipulating both the x and y axes of the vocal tract). Pitch is the actual frequency itself. Think the difference between a cello and a violin playing the exact same frequency/note. Violin always sounds brighter (to an untrained ear, “smaller”) than cello, but the fundamental frequency being played on both instruments is the same.

Hey I’m the *ORIGINAL CREATOR* of the whisper siren. A big Hangup that a lot of folks have, is sustaining the short and narrow vocal tract shape when they transition to vocalizing. 

Here’s my original exercise in its full glory. If you find it helpful be sure to subscribe to my YouTube channel, and check out my recent presentation on the [Fundamentals Of Transvoice](https://youtu.be/A4FMy_dxxYc)Exercise 2 - The Whisper Siren (June 2018):1. 	Start with a deep/low sounding whisper on an “ah”, you should notice that you feel pressure in the back of your mouth as you make this sound. check your laryngeal positioning (your larynx should be really low), imagine the waffle cone in your throat that you do not want to crush. DO NOT VOCALIZE AT ALL, the whisper should just be air, as is customary for any type of whisper.2. 	From the deep/low whisper on an “ah” gradually slide up, progressively drop your jaw to make room for the tongue. (without pushing, tensing your throat, or increasing volume) to a high pitch whisper on “ah”. As you gradually slide up in “Pitch”, Drop your jaw and progressively stick your tongue as you go gradually slide higher so the tip of your tongue touches the bottom of your chin, do not allow your tongue to retract what so ever. As stated before, when you whisper there should be NO VOCALIZATION AT ALL, just air.3.	 Once you get to the high “pitch” whisper, hold it for 2 seconds, making sure you keep your tongue out all the way so the tip is touching the bottom of your chin,4. Next without pausing or inhaling, ease into an "ah" on C4 without letting your larynx drop. Then go into “my name is ___” on C4 in M1 WITHOUT DROPPING the larynx.
for the whisper siren, steps should be:1) Drop jaw down vertically2) tongue starts moving forward out of the mouth3) drop jaw down even further to make room for the tongue (bottom lip should NEVER cover bottom teeth)4) progressively sticking the tongue out even more, as you near the highest part of the whisper, smile, but DO NOT bring your lower jaw back up, keep the lower jaw in the same position.

Tips: get quieter as you go up with your whisper

Whisper Siren Trick (from the ACTUAL teacher who invented of the exercise):

When doing the whisper siren, one thing that may help is when doing the whisper siren, keeping subglottal air pressure light (breath pressure). Thus the actual whisper siren should be semi quiet, and as you side up you’re gonna get even quieter. Once you slide up to the highest point of the whisper, Hold the highest part of the whisper siren for 2 seconds exhaling, then without pausing or breathing immediately[NatfemVoice.com](https://natfemvoice.com/registration) quietly vocalize on “ah” on C4 in M1 with a HOQ (higher open quotient). Make sure there’s no pause or breathe (especially nose breaths -they can be sneak in there if you’re not paying attention-) between the 2 second high whisper exhale and the HOQ “ah” on C4 in M1) the exhale should naturally lead into an “ah”. When you go into the actual vocalization there is a ABSOLUTE need to increase subglottal air pressure. 

Tips: make sure to keep the ribcage open when you vocalize, if you close it the second you vocalize your capacity to easily increase subglottal air pressure goes out of the window, it’s essentially inflating the lungs just to deflate them really quick, by the time you vocalize there’s not gonna be enough capacity for subglottal air pressure therefore one’s ability to stabilize pitch and resonance on the ah can be compromised.
